title: Cisplatin + etoposide + chest radiotherapy
purpose: Chemotherapy and chest radiotherapy work together to treat lung cancer. Your team will explain the aim, possible benefit and alternatives for you.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin damages the DNA that cancer cells need to divide. It can also affect healthy cells.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, reduced urine, hearing changes or tingling.

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with an enzyme used to copy and repair DNA. This can stop cancer cells growing and can also lower healthy blood counts.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, a sore mouth or feeling faint during an infusion.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Infusion reaction or low blood pressure

agents.name: Chest radiotherapy
agents.explanation: Radiotherapy directs radiation at the planned chest area. Its appointments and dose are set by the radiation oncology team.
agents.watch: Report painful swallowing, poor intake, skin changes, new cough or breathlessness.
risks: Sore skin in the treated area
Cough or breathing changes during or after treatment

phases.label: Two initial cycles with radiotherapy
phases.detail: Cisplatin on Days 1 and 8; etoposide on Days 1–5. Radiation appointments run alongside chemotherapy as planned by radiation oncology.

phases.label: Review before any further cycles
phases.detail: If the cancer has not progressed and treatment remains appropriate, the consultant may prescribe two additional cycles with an agreed radiation plan. These are not automatic.

phases.label: Recovery and next treatment decision
phases.detail: Your team reviews recovery and response, then agrees the next plan. Further drug treatment or surgery is a separate decision.

timeline.label: Etoposide only
timeline.text: A separate infusion on each of Days 2,3,4 and 5, with prescribed safety checks.

timeline.label: Radiotherapy: separate appointment plan
timeline.text: This band shows overlap with the chemotherapy cycle, not daily radiation or a fixed number of fractions. Follow your radiation calendar.

timeline.label: Check symptoms throughout
timeline.text: Symptoms can arise on any day, including after the last treatment.

day_groups.title: Both chemotherapy medicines
day_groups.body: Treatment after blood-test and symptom review. Radiotherapy usually begins close to this first treatment.
day_groups.action: Confirm both treatment plans and take only the prescribed support medicines.

day_groups.title: Etoposide each day
day_groups.body: Return for etoposide on each of these four days. Radiotherapy appointments may also be planned.
day_groups.action: The team checks blood results and symptoms before dosing. Report swallowing or breathing changes.

day_groups.title: No planned chemotherapy
day_groups.body: Follow the separate radiotherapy calendar. Anti-sickness medicines may continue as prescribed.
day_groups.action: Call if unwell; do not wait for the next infusion.

day_groups.title: Cisplatin only
day_groups.body: Return for the second cisplatin dose after safety checks. Extra drip fluids are needed; etoposide is not given today.
day_groups.action: Confirm today’s anti-sickness plan with the team.

day_groups.title: No further chemotherapy this cycle
day_groups.body: Continue any planned radiotherapy appointments and safety checks. Tiredness and swallowing symptoms can build up.
day_groups.action: Report new symptoms and keep the urgent contact plan available, including after treatment ends.

support.title: Your anti-sickness plan
support.text: Cisplatin days need a different plan from etoposide-only days. The team combines prevention and rescue medicines into one clear schedule. Do not repeat or add courses yourself.

support.title: Eating, drinking and swallowing
support.text: Report painful swallowing, weight loss or difficulty drinking early. The team can arrange pain relief, dietitian support or other help.

support.title: Fluids and kidney protection
support.text: Follow your individual drinking advice and report much less urine. Cisplatin needs drip fluids before and after dosing; tell staff if you cannot drink or feel swollen or breathless.

support.title: Other medicines and prevention
support.text: Bring a full medicine list. Ask before starting medicines, supplements or vaccines. Fertility and contraception advice should be agreed before treatment.

questions.a: Chemotherapy is planned on Days 1–5 and8 of each cycle. Radiotherapy has a separate appointment calendar; do not use this cycle diagram as the radiation timetable.

questions.q: How many cycles will I have?
questions.a: Two cycles are planned. Two further cycles may be offered only after review and a new confirmed plan.

questions.q: Can side effects continue after treatment?
questions.a: Yes. Keep reporting new or worsening symptoms after the last infusion or radiation session. The team agrees your follow-up checks.

evidence.title: Understanding the evidence
evidence.intro: Chemotherapy and radiotherapy are used together for selected people with Stage III lung cancer.
evidence.interpretation: Published results help guide discussion but do not predict your outcome. The source study was small and did not compare this regimen with another treatment.

indication_text: NCCP 00456a: Stage III non-small-cell lung cancer
schedule_summary: Cisplatin on Days 1 and 8; etoposide on Days 1–5. Each cycle lasts 28 days. Two cycles first; two more may be offered after review. Radiotherapy usually starts within 24 hours of the first chemotherapy dose; follow your separate radiation appointment plan.
administration_text: Cisplatin 50 mg/m² over 1 hour with pre/post hydration on Days 1 and 8; etoposide 50 mg/m² over1 hour on each of Days 1–5. Visits also include safety checks and preparation. The radiation team confirms its separate dose, fractions and calendar.
monitoring_summary: Before starting: full blood count, kidney and liver tests; hearing tests and creatinine clearance if clinically indicated. During treatment: NCCP blood counts on Days 1 and 8; etoposide product information adds blood counts before each etoposide dose, including Days 2–5. Kidney and liver tests before each cycle. Extra tests and response scans follow the individual plan.

monitoring_schedule.title: My tests and checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Required safety tests are distinct from team-agreed scans and follow-up. Radiotherapy appointments and extra tests follow your personal plan.

urgent_extra: Call oncology immediately for fever, sudden illness, new or worsening breathlessness, troublesome bleeding, inability to drink or swallow, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine or severe rash. Tell staff at once about pain, swelling, faintness or breathing trouble during an infusion.
consent_support: Discuss the aim and alternatives, blood-count suppression and serious infection, kidney/hearing/nerve injury, nausea, hair loss, infusion reactions, fertility, and chest radiation effects including swallowing and breathing problems. Etoposide for NSCLC is outside its licensed indication; explain the rationale and follow local off-label consent policy.

sections.title: Before the first visit
sections.text: Confirm both oncology teams, treatment and test appointments, medicines, transport and urgent contacts.

sections.title: Frequent visits in week 1
sections.text: Plan for chemotherapy on Days 1–5 plus Day 8. Radiation may require other visits; combine calendars with the team.

sections.title: After the visits
sections.text: Keep support medicines and contact numbers at hand. Ask early for help with swallowing, food, fluids or transport.

anatomy: Report ringing in the ears, hearing change or new tingling.
Report mouth sores, painful swallowing or difficulty drinking.
New or worsening cough or breathlessness needs prompt advice, during or after treatment.
Report much less urine, swelling or trouble drinking.
Fever, chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding need immediate advice.
Tell the team about sore skin in the treated area, a spreading rash or increasing fatigue.

chronology_notes.title: Two overlapping plans
chronology_notes.text: Chemotherapy days do not define the radiation schedule. Follow the written radiation calendar even on a day without chemotherapy.

chronology_notes.title: Symptoms can build up
chronology_notes.text: Tiredness and swallowing discomfort may develop during treatment. Breathing changes can also appear later; report them after treatment as well.

timeline_note: Relative chemotherapy days only. Radiotherapy band shows overlap, not a daily dose or fraction count. There is no guaranteed safe day for symptoms.
safety_note: Call oncology immediately for fever, sudden illness, new or worsening breathlessness, troublesome bleeding, inability to drink or swallow, uncontrolled vomiting, very little urine or severe rash. Tell staff at once about pain, swelling, faintness or breathing trouble during an infusion.
passport_visit_note: Record actual treatment dates, delays and omitted doses. A completed cycle includes all planned chemotherapy doses; it does not approve the next dose or record each radiation fraction.
treatment_scope_notice: This guide is for Stage III non-small-cell lung cancer. Your radiation team supplies the exact radiation calendar; later treatment is a separate decision.
phases_note: The team confirms dates, radiation fractions and any optional phase.
anatomy_note: Selected effects from chemotherapy and chest radiotherapy; symptoms can have more than one cause.
teachback: Which chemotherapy days will I attend?
Who will I ring if unwell tonight?

patient_summary.purpose: Chemotherapy and chest radiotherapy work together to treat lung cancer. Your team will explain the aim, possible benefit and alternatives for you.
patient_summary.schedule: Cisplatin on Days 1 and 8; etoposide on Days 1–5. Each cycle lasts 28 days. Two cycles first; two more may be offered after review. Radiotherapy usually starts within 24 hours of the first chemotherapy dose; follow your separate radiation appointment plan.

phases.title: Chemotherapy + radiotherapy
phases.text: Two 28-day chemotherapy cycles; radiation runs alongside on its own appointment plan.

phases.title: Review
phases.text: Two more cycles only if prescribed after review; not automatic.

phases.title: After treatment
phases.text: Recovery checks and the next treatment decision follow your individual plan.

preparation: Bring your medicine list and both treatment calendars.
Confirm tests, support medicines and urgent contacts before leaving.
patient_summary.card_schedule: 28-day cycles: Cisplatin D1/8; etoposide D1–5; chest RT. 2 cycles, then review.
patient_summary.card_alert: Show this card when seeking care. Fever or sudden illness needs prompt oncology advice.

monitoring.when: Before first treatment; hearing / clearance tests if needed
Days 1 and 8; also before each etoposide dose
Before each cycle; extra checks if unwell. Review swallowing and breathing.
Team-agreed follow-up; no fixed scan or tumour-marker interval in this regimen.

cycle_expectations: Tiredness, sickness or swallowing discomfort can occur; report difficulty eating or drinking early.
Report fever or new breathing changes at any time, including after treatment.
